title: Test both self-closing gates, tag the one that stays open, and leave both shut
instruction: Check that each gate shuts by itself after you open it and let go. Put the red tag on the white pad beside any gate that does not, and leave both gates shut.
context: Self-closing gates guard the access openings in guardrails around ladderway holes (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.29(b)(13)(i)): the drop is beyond the fence and the gate swings away from it. A gate whose closer has failed stays open, leaves the drop unguarded, and looks like one that works. An inspector opens each gate, lets go, tags the one that stays open and shuts it. Unlike TK-U2GEMP and TK-93R4YG, this tests a return seen only after letting go, and ends with the barrier made safe.
setup: A scale model of a guard fence on the station table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart): x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. All parts are rigid painted plastic. Fence line: centre plane at x 33.0. Two gates, one in front of each arm, identical in look and size, with yellow leaves. Each has a dark grey hinge post (cylinder 24 mm diameter, 110 mm tall) at (33.0, +19.5) for the left gate and (33.0, -19.5) for the right gate, and a yellow leaf 10 mm thick, 120 mm wide and 80 mm tall, its bottom 10 mm above the table. When shut, the leaf lies along the fence from 1.0 to 13.0 cm inboard of its hinge axis (y +18.5 to +6.5 on the left, -18.5 to -6.5 on the right). A black knob post (cylinder 16 mm diameter, 45 mm tall, 75 to 120 mm above the table) stands on the leaf's centre line, 10.5 cm from the hinge axis. Each leaf weighs 100 g with its knob and swings toward the robot, from 0 (shut) to 92 degrees open. A dark grey latch post, 20 x 20 x 90 mm tall, stands just past each free end (y +4.5 to +6.5 and -4.5 to -6.5). The left gate has a working closer: a torsion spring of 0.1 N m per radian, pre-loaded so it presses the gate shut with 0.05 N m (0.13 N m at 45 degrees open), hinge damping 0.05 N m s/rad. The right gate's closer has failed: no spring, hinge damping 0.3 N m s/rad, so it stays where it is left. Fixed grey fence panels, 10 mm thick and 90 mm tall, in the fence plane: one between the latch posts (y -4.5 to +4.5) and one outward of each hinge post (|y| 20.7 to 30.0). Fixed white pads, 60 x 60 x 2 mm, glued to the table, centred at (27.0, +25.0) beside the left gate and (27.0, -25.0) beside the right gate. Red tag: a loose 30 mm cube, 20 g, standing at (17.0, 0). Both gates start shut. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from the video and a photo with a protractor and ruler. A gate is shut when it is within 5 degrees of its latch post. The tag is on a pad when it is released and at rest, lying flat (a face within 10 degrees of level), its bottom within 1 mm of the pad's top, and seen from above all of it is on the 60 x 60 mm pad. The left gate counts as tested when it went from at least 15 degrees open to 5 degrees or less while the right gate was still (under 0.1 degree per control step). The right gate counts as tested when it stood at least 15 degrees open, unmoving (under 0.1 degree per step), for 1 s. The tag must be placed after both gates were tested: if it touched either pad (its bottom within 5 mm of the pad's top over any part of it) before then, the trial scores 0. At the end: 1.0 if both gates were tested, the tag is on the right gate's pad and both gates are shut; 0 otherwise, including either gate more than 5 degrees open, the tag on the left gate's pad, the table or anything else, held or moving, placed before testing, or either gate not tested. Trial ends once 1.0 has held for 3 s.
reset_notes: Shut both gates and stand the tag back at (17.0, 0), square to the table edges. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: A scale model (about 1:10) of a guard fence with two swing gates, built from rigid boxes and cylinders. Each gate turns on an ideal hinge with stops at shut and 92 degrees open; the working closer is a pre-loaded torsion spring, and the failed one is simply absent, with stiffer hinge damping. Shut means against the stop; no latch is modelled. The tag is a red block set on a pad beside the gate, standing in for a tag hung on it.
